title: In the beginning
body:
Good morning!

Day 1.

Here we go. Genesis 1.

Read it slowly. Notice how much of this chapter is God simply speaking, and how the speaking is enough.

Nothing has gone wrong yet. Nobody has sinned or run or hidden. This is just God making things and calling them good.

That is where He wants us to start.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The garden
body:
Good morning!

Day 2.

Today the camera zooms in. Chapter 1 was the whole universe. Chapter 2 is one garden and one man.

Watch what God does here. He plants a garden, walks in it, and notices that the man is alone. Then He does something about it.

The God who spoke galaxies into place gets His hands dirty.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The fall
body:
Good morning!

Day 3.

Everything breaks today.

But read carefully what God does after it breaks. He comes looking for them, asking questions He already knows the answer to, and before He sends them out He makes them clothes.

Judgment and kindness in the same chapter, from the same God.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Cain and Abel
body:
Good morning!

Day 4.

The first murder, one chapter after the first sin.

Before Cain does anything, God warns him. Sin is crouching at your door, He says, and you must rule over it. Cain does not listen.

And even after, God marks him for protection instead of leaving him to whatever was coming.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The long line, and the earth goes wrong
body:
Good morning!

Day 5.

Chapter 5 is a list of names and ages and it is easy to skim. Try not to. Somebody lived every one of those lines.

Then chapter 6 says something worth stopping on. God's heart was deeply troubled. He grieved.

Not distant. Grieved.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The flood, and the waters go down
body:
Good morning!

Day 6.

This is a hard chapter to read slowly. The water takes everything, and the story does not soften it. Do not rush past that to get to the dove.

But watch the small line at the start of chapter 8. God remembered Noah. It does not mean He had forgotten. It means He turned toward him.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The rainbow, and the nations
body:
Good morning!

Day 7.

God makes a promise and then hangs the sign of it in the sky, pointed where He can see it rather than where we can.

Chapter 10 is a long list of nations and it is tempting to skim. Read it as a map of where everybody went after the water.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Babel, and the line that leads to Abram
body:
Good morning!

Day 8.

Babel is a tower built so somebody could make a name for themselves.

Notice that God comes down to look at it. The tower meant to reach heaven was so small He had to come down to see it.

Then the chapter ends quietly, with a family nobody had heard of.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Leave your country
body:
Good morning!

Day 9.

Leave your country and your father's house and go to a land I will show you. No map. No details about where.

Abram goes.

And then, once he gets there, he lets Lot pick the good land first.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Count the stars
body:
Good morning!

Day 10.

God takes Abram outside at night and tells him to count the stars. Abram is old and has no children at all.

He also asks God how can I know. He says it straight out.

God does not scold him for asking. He answers him.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Hagar, and the new names
body:
Good morning!

Day 11.

Hagar is a slave with no power and no say in any of it, and she is the first person in the whole Bible to give God a name.

You are the God who sees me.

She says it in a desert, running away, pregnant and alone.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Three visitors, and Abraham argues with God
body:
Good morning!

Day 12.

Abraham bargains with God over a city, and God lets him do it. Fifty, then forty five, all the way down to ten.

Read it slowly and notice that God never gets impatient with him.

It tells you something about what He is willing to sit and hear.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Sodom, and Lot
body:
Good morning!

Day 13.

Today is a hard chapter, and I am not going to tidy it up for you. Sodom burns. Then Lot's daughters do something awful in a cave, and nobody in the whole chapter comes out of it well.

Read it anyway.

God is not embarrassed by what is in His own book, and He did not clean up the family He rescued before letting us see them.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Isaac laughs
body:
Good morning!

Day 14.

Sarah laughed when she heard she would have a son, and she laughed because it was ridiculous.

God named the boy Laughter.

He did not correct her for it. He gave her the joke back, and this time she laughed out loud in front of everybody.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The mountain
body:
Good morning!

Day 15.

Three days walking. That is the part nobody mentions. Abraham had three whole days to think about what he was going to the mountain to do.

Read it slowly. Do not skip ahead to the ram in the thicket.

Sit in the three days, because Abraham had to.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Burying Sarah, finding Rebekah
body:
Good morning!

Day 16.

Abraham buries his wife, and to do it he has to buy a field. That cave is the only piece of land he ever owns in the country God promised him.

Then a servant prays a very specific prayer at a well, and watches it get answered while he is still praying.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Two nations, one bowl of stew
body:
Good morning!

Day 17.

Esau sells what was his for a bowl of stew, because he is hungry right now and now feels like the only thing that is real.

Jacob is already grasping at his brother's heel.

Neither of these men is impressive. God keeps working with them anyway.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The stolen blessing, and the ladder
body:
Good morning!

Day 18.

Jacob lies to his blind father and steals what was never his. Then he runs for his life.

And on the night he is running, with a stone for a pillow and nothing to his name, God stands at the top of a staircase and makes him a promise.

Not a lecture. A promise.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Leah, Rachel, and twelve sons
body:
Good morning!

Day 19.

Leah is the unloved one and she knows it.

Watch the names she gives her sons. They read like a diary of what she is hoping for.

By the fourth one she stops naming them after what she wants from her husband, and names him Praise.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Wrestling until daybreak
body:
Good morning!

Day 20.

Jacob wrestles somebody until daybreak and will not let go until he is blessed.

He walks away from that night with a new name and a limp.

And he got exactly what he asked for. He never walked the same way again.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Facing Esau, and Dinah
body:
Good morning!

Day 21.

The reunion with Esau goes better than Jacob had any right to expect.

Then chapter 34 happens, and it is ugly. Dinah is violated, and her brothers answer with slaughter.

God is not quoted once in that chapter. Sometimes the silence is the thing to notice.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Back to Bethel
body:
Good morning!

Day 22.

God tells Jacob to go back to Bethel, which is the place with the staircase, the place it all started.

So he goes back to the beginning.

Rachel dies on the road there. The chapter carries both things at once and does not explain itself.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The coat, and the pit
body:
Good morning!

Day 23.

Joseph is seventeen and honestly not very likeable. His father plays favourites in front of everybody, and his brothers hate him for it.

By the end of the chapter he is in a dry well, listening to them eat lunch, and then on a road to Egypt.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Judah and Tamar
body:
Good morning!

Day 24.

Genesis stops the Joseph story here to tell you about Judah and Tamar, and it is not a comfortable read.

A widow with no protection does something desperate, because the man who owed her had done nothing.

Judah is the one in the wrong, and to his credit he says so out loud. This chapter is in here on purpose. Tamar ends up in the family line of Jesus.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Prison, and dreams
body:
Good morning!

Day 25.

Joseph does the right thing and is punished for it. Then he is forgotten in a prison for two more years.

Watch the small sentence the chapter keeps repeating. The Lord was with Joseph.

It says that while he is a slave. It says it again while he is a prisoner.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: From the dungeon to the palace
body:
Good morning!

Day 26.

Joseph goes from a cell to second in command of Egypt inside a single day.

Notice what he says before he interprets anything at all.

I cannot do it, but God will.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The brothers come, twice
body:
Good morning!

Day 27.

The brothers stand in front of Joseph and have no idea who he is. He knows exactly who they are.

Watch how long he takes, and what he does when he has to leave the room because he is about to cry.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: I am Joseph
body:
Good morning!

Day 28.

I am Joseph. Is my father still alive.

He has had years to prepare a speech and that is what comes out of him.

Then he tells them not to be angry with themselves, which is a strange and generous thing to say to the men who sold you.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: Down to Egypt, and a blessing
body:
Good morning!

Day 29.

Jacob is old and he is moving to Egypt, which is the last place he expected to end up.

God tells him not to be afraid to go, and promises to bring him back.

Then a dying man blesses two grandsons he has never met, and crosses his hands to do it.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: You meant evil, God meant good
body:
Good morning!

Day 30.

You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good.

Joseph says it to the brothers who sold him. Not that it was not evil. That God was working the whole time it was.

The book ends with a coffin in Egypt and a promise that has not come true yet.

One line before you close it. What did this show you about God?

Heather

title: The whole timeline, and where Moses walks in
body:
Good morning!

Day 31.

You read the whole thing. All fifty chapters, from the first light to a coffin in Egypt.

Scroll down and read your own lines back. That list is what this month was actually for.

Genesis ends unfinished on purpose. A family is sitting in Egypt, a promise is still outstanding, and four hundred years later a baby gets put in a basket in a river.

That is where Moses walks in.

Heather
